## Exercise 4.1: Build it — a diagonal cart {#ex-4.1}

`addCart` only moves along one axis, so make this one by hand, in the same group:

```js
const diagonal = this.carts.create(at(20), at(11), 'cart'); // <1>
diagonal.setBounce(1).setCollideWorldBounds(true).setPushable(false);
diagonal.setVelocity(120, 90); // <2>
```
1. Because it's in `this.carts`, it's already covered by every collider set up for carts: walls, the freezer, the player. That's the point of groups: add to the group, get the rules for free.
2. Velocity on both axes. With `setBounce(1)` it reflects off whatever it hits and never loses speed.

Bouncing off the freezer needs nothing extra: the scene already has `this.physics.add.collider(this.carts, this.freezer)`.

{{< game solutions/04/ex-4.1 caption="A third cart, bouncing diagonally." >}}

The full file is in `solutions/04/ex-4.1/`.

## Exercise 4.2: Predict it — a solid sample {#ex-4.2}

It still works: `collider` calls its callback when the bodies touch, just like `overlap`. But you **bump into** the sample first. The researcher stops for a moment against the tube before it disappears, because the collider separates the bodies in the same step it calls you back.

Here it's subtle, because `pickUp` hides the tube at once. With something you don't remove (the drop zone), a collider would stop you dead in front of the freezer and you could never walk "into" the zone. Pickups, triggers and zones are overlaps. Use a collider only for things that should be solid.

## Exercise 4.3: Spot the bug — the runaway cart {#ex-4.3}

`setPushable(false)` is missing.

Two dynamic bodies that collide push each other apart, sharing the push. When the researcher walks into the side of a cart, the cart gets some of the researcher's velocity, sideways to its lane. With `setBounce(1)` it never loses that speed, so it carries on diagonally forever.

```js
cart.setBounce(1).setCollideWorldBounds(true).setPushable(false);
```

With `pushable` off, the cart still collides with everything, but only the *other* body moves when they meet.

You might reach for `setImmovable(true)` instead. That also stops the shove, but an immovable body isn't moved by **any** collision. Walls are immovable too, and when two immovable bodies meet, neither gives way, so the cart drives straight through the wall and out of the room. `pushable` is the narrower switch, and the right one here.

## Exercise 4.4: Tune it — ice rink or office floor {#ex-4.4}

| Feel | What to change | Try |
|---|---|---|
| **Ice** | Drag, way down. Acceleration down a bit. | drag 80, acceleration 600 |
| **Heavy** | Acceleration down, max speed down, drag medium | acceleration 400, max 150, drag 900 |
| **Twitchy** | Acceleration and drag both very high | acceleration 5000, drag 6000 |

- **Drag** decides how long you slide after letting go. It's the "ice" number: *Cold Chain*'s spills drop it to 90.
- **Acceleration** decides how long it takes to reach full speed. Low acceleration is what makes something feel heavy.
- **Max speed** is the speed, but on its own it changes "fast or slow", not "how it feels".

Most action games sit at the twitchy end for the player (you want control) and give other things more weight. Lesson 8 moves all of these numbers into one tuning file.
